items.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
items.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added a high-severity security flaw impacting UnrealIRCd, an open-source Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following reports of active exploitation. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of improper neutralization of delimiters

items.title: FBI Reveals How Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents to Gain Privileged Access in Under Three Hours
items.description: The FBI has warned that hackers are using ARTEX AI agents to automate network attacks, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. Its November 13, 2026, FLASH alert describes how attackers combine stolen credentials, exposed applications, and cloud permissions to shorten the gap between discovery and compromise. items.title: Apple Reveals How Secure Exclaves Shield Camera and Microphone Data
items.description: The tech giant has detailed the architecture designed to isolate ambient sensor data from the main OS on HomeView and new iPhones. The post Apple Reveals How Secure Exclaves Shield Camera and Microphone Data appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Microsoft Warns of Active Password Stealing Attack Exploiting the Microsoft 365 Service Disruption
items.description: Microsoft has warned of an active phishing campaign using the November 12 Microsoft 365 service disruption to lure users into opening fake email recovery links. The messages copy Microsoft service health notices and cite the real Exchange Online incident EX1550543, making the requests appear linked to an ongoing business problem. items.title: Cursor Reveals How a Leaked Fireworks AI Key Led to a Backdoored Claude Code Extension
items.description: Cursor has traced its October security breach to an access key exposed by Fireworks AI. The attacker used that key to steal historical coding agent records, find more credentials, and eventually place backdoored Claude Code extensions in Cursor’s marketplace cache. items.title: No Signs of Hacking in FAA Ground Stop as FBI Reportedly Probes Software Update
items.description: Officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack behind the nationwide FAA outage, which may have been caused by a software update. The post No Signs of Hacking in FAA Ground Stop as FBI Reportedly Probes Software Update appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: CISA Warns of Check Point 0-Day Vulnerability Exploited to Gain Root Access
items.description: CISA has warned that attackers are exploiting a Check Point security flaw that lets a local user gain root access on affected appliances. items.title: Uber Confirms Data Breach – Hackers Stole Users’ Personal Information
items.description: Uber has confirmed a data breach involving the personal information of thousands of U.S. drivers after hackers accessed records held by Fireworks AI, a third-party technology provider. The exposed information includes driver’s license details. Uber is notifying affected people, but it has not disclosed the total number impacted nationwide. items.description: Federal officials have yet to say what caused the communications disruption or whether they are investigating a possible cyberattack. The post FAA Ground Stop Issued Due to ‘Extraordinary Circumstances’ appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
items.description: Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Trezor has confirmed that three Safe 5 devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to steal wallet recovery phrases and send them to attackers over cellular networks. [...]
